description: The embedded DEFAULT extension pack -- a generic, workspace-agnostic vocabulary that instantiates `frontmatter-core.schema.json` (core@1) with a minimal, broadly-applicable tagging scheme: the six required fields + their fix-tier authorship, description caps by file_class, the `type`/`status`/`topic` namespace vocabulary, the file_class classification globs, and a small generated/exempt taxonomy. Carries NO report vocabulary -- the report namespaces (`source`/`period`/`audience`/`cadence`) and the report rule-set live only in the separate, opt-in `reports@1` pack. A repo layers this pack (optionally with `reports@1` and its own domain-specific pack) via its `navigator.toml`, or replaces it outright with its own vocabulary.

required_fields.source: A semantic title -- not mechanically inferable.
Routing prose, capped by file_class (see description_caps).
A stable identity string -- not mechanically inferable.
Classification judgement -- a fix pass can only repair structure, not choose topics.
Relationship judgement -- which other documents this one relates to.
An ISO-8601 UTC timestamp -- stampable at fix time.

description_caps.source: Description length cap by file class: context/workspace docs stay tightest since they're read most often; Skills and Agents get progressively more room for the extra routing detail their frontmatter carries.

rules.source: Each skill is a `SKILL.md` under `.claude/skills/<name>/`; the skill file-class description cap is wider than a plain context doc's.
Any `SKILL.md` anywhere is a skill (broad fallback after the anchored rule).
One `.md` per subagent under `.claude/agents/`; the agent file-class description cap is the widest.

file_class.note: Rules evaluated in array order, first match wins, else `default`. Globs use fnmatch semantics (`*` spans `/`); the anchored skill rule precedes the broad `**/SKILL.md` rule so both a nested and a repo-root SKILL.md classify as skill. `default=context` covers every other document (the tightest description-cap class).

namespaces.name: type
namespaces.source: Exactly one document-kind tag per file.

namespaces.name: status
namespaces.source: Exactly one completeness tag per file.

namespaces.name: topic
namespaces.source: One or more subject-area tags per file.

namespaces_order_note: Array order IS the cascade iteration order (core `violation_cascade`): singletons type,status; at_least_one topic. Reordering this array changes emitted violation order for a multi-violation file -- treat it as a behavior change, not a cosmetic one.

report.notes: Interim placeholder: `core@1`'s meta-schema/struct still require a `report` block on every pack, but this pack carries no report vocabulary (that's `reports@1`'s job, M1.P1.T2) -- so `trigger.value` names no real tag any document uses, `required_namespaces` is empty, and `period` points at an always-present namespace with a no-op regex. Dormant when this pack is layered alone; a repo that also layers `reports@1` gets that pack's real trigger/period, which wins the merge. Retired once `core@2` (M1.P3.T1) generalizes `report` into a `{match, apply}` construct with no report-named special case.
report.source: Placeholder mechanics only -- see `notes`. The real report axis lives in `reports@1`.

exempt.source: A minimal generated/exempt taxonomy: common cache/VCS directories and a few conventional filenames every repo tends to have. An adopting repo's own pack typically adds path_globs for its own generated-content locations.
